note: Single source of truth for what the schema is expected to look like, before and after the first Flyway-enabled boot. The quality gate must never hardcode these numbers in a workflow: it reads this file through ops/quality/checks/verify-schema-state.ps1, which picks the profile by asking the database whether flyway_schema_history exists. If neither profile matches, the gate FAILS — it never falls back to 'no assertion'.
owner: the database agent maintains the numbers; Agent L (quality) consumes them

chain.note: The first Spring boot stamps the baseline and then applies twenty-five additive migrations. Before that boot `firstelement` has no flyway_schema_history row at all. ALL twenty-five are transactional: there is no .conf sidecar anywhere in the chain and no non-transactional script. V20261005120000 uses a plain CREATE INDEX rather than CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY because flyway-core 11.7.2 Community has no per-script executeInTransaction override, and a CONCURRENTLY-only migration HANGS on Flyway's own schema-history advisory-lock transaction; see docs/migration/flyway-runbook.md section 9c and the migration's own header. The last five versions (20261006100000..20261006140000) are the Phase-10b schema remediation batch and are described in docs/migration/phases/phase-10b-schema-remediation.md. The last two versions of that group (20261007100000..20261007110000) are the Phase-14 P0 customer reference namespace batch (ADR-0014, defect CX-1). The final three versions are V20261007110000 (Phase-14 customer cxId tenant rescope), V20261009110000 (Phase-35 composite tenant foreign keys on appointments) and V20261009130000 (Phase-38, ONE enum VALUE: CLINIC_STAFF on "UserRole"); see docs/migration/phases/phase-38-clinic-staff-and-contract-truth.md.

preBoot.description: The verified live database as it exists before any Flyway stamp: the Phase-2 baseline only, created by `prisma db push`, with no migration history.

postBoot.description: After the first Flyway-enabled boot: the baseline stamped, then twenty-four additive migrations applied — the vector index, the Phase-5a outbox/job/idempotency slice, the Phase-6a workflow/SLA/collision slice, the Phase-7-10a audit, report, export, usage-ledger, finance, AI-governance and AI-run-child-scope slice, the Phase-10b schema remediation batch (two constraint corrections, one composite tenant FK, two credential tables, one privacy subject reference), and the Phase-14 P0 customer reference namespace batch (one per-organization counter table, the atomic allocator, the counter backfill from max(cxId), and cxId uniqueness rescoped from global to per-organization), and the Phase-35 appointment tenant batch (four composite tenant FKs on appointments, plus the two target indexes doctors and procedures lacked).
postBoot.establishedBy: phase-38, re-measured against a disposable database created from template0 and carrying the WHOLE 26-migration chain applied in ONE psql session (ops/flyway/verification/verify-clean-bootstrap.ps1), which is the shape Flyway produces on a single connection and the only shape under which the baseline's search_path = '' is in force for migrations 2..26. MEASURED, not derived, on PostgreSQL 16.15. PHASE 38 CHANGED THE FINGERPRINT AND NOT ONE COUNT. V20261009130000 adds a single enum VALUE to the EXISTING "UserRole" type, so tableCount stays 98, enumCount stays 57 (that figure counts enum TYPES, not labels), checkCount stays 422, and FKs/indexes/unique indexes/PKs/triggers/nullable projectId are all untouched. A fingerprint move with a frozen census is the correct signature of this change and is exactly why it was worth measuring rather than predicting: the phase-35 value 896f371b51d192ca9bf19643e0cb4443 is now historical. PHASE 38 ALSO FOUND, IN ITS OWN FIRST DRAFT, THE DEFECT CLASS PHASE 30 FOUND IN SIX GUARDS: a `role_type regtype := '"UserRole"'::regtype` DECLARE default, and then an unqualified `ALTER TYPE "UserRole"`, both of which resolve to nothing under the chain's search_path = '' and both of which failed the clean-bootstrap rehearsal as `type "UserRole" does not exist`. The probe that had passed them ran the setup and the migration in TWO SEPARATE psql sessions and so never reproduced the one-session condition the chain actually runs under. Fixed with to_regtype('public."UserRole"') -- which returns NULL instead of raising, so the existence question is answerable inside the block at all -- and a qualified ALTER TYPE public."UserRole". Both copies of the chain are byte-identical.

alsoMeasured.indexCensus: 209 tenant-led / 15 project-led / 22 parent-key / 142 unique-other / 5 global / 1 vector-led
triggerFunctions: firstelement_api_key_hash_guard (api_keys) — Phase 10b, refuses a plaintext-shaped keyHash
firstelement_principal_lifecycle_audit (api_keys, service_principals) — Phase 10b, writes admin_audit_events on a credential lifecycle change
phase10bConstraints: ai_approvals_approval_check — REPLACED: (status IN ('APPROVED','REJECTED','REVOKED')) = (decidedAt IS NOT NULL). ADR-0011 §1 states the required form with only APPROVED and REJECTED; 'REVOKED' was added because ai_approvals_decision_pair_check is a biconditional, so a REVOKED row that keeps WHO granted it must also keep decidedAt, and without it ADR-0011 §1 rule 4 stays unimplementable. 'EXPIRED' was deliberately NOT added: PENDING->EXPIRED means nobody decided it. Deviation recorded in docs/migration/phases/phase-10b-schema-remediation.md.

legal_holds_scope_pair_check — REPLACED: every LegalHoldScopeType member now has a satisfiable arm (TENANT no scopeRef / PROJECT must name a project / TABLE+RECORD must name a non-blank scopeRef). Purely a widening; the repair count is necessarily and measurably 0.

document_chunks_document_tenant_fkey — NEW: FOREIGN KEY (documentId, organizationId) -> documents(id, organizationId) ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE CASCADE. The pre-existing single-column document_chunks_documentId_fkey is KEPT on purpose (redundant but its CASCADE is the deletion-propagation contract Phase 10 asserts).

privacy_deletion_requests_subject_reference_check — NEW: a USER/EMPLOYEE subject names subjectUserId, a CUSTOMER names subjectCustomerId, a TENANT names neither, and the two references are never both set. Carries a deliberately labelled LEGACY arm (CUSTOMER + subjectUserId) so existing rows keep satisfying a CHECK; removed by follow-up F-3 once its count is 0.
correctionsForcedByTheFixture: ai_tool_registry_risk_field_list_check: array_length('{}',1) is NULL and NULL>=1 is NULL, so the empty-allow-list guard was satisfied by every empty allow-list. Now coalesce(array_length(...),0)>=1.

finance_periods_locked_check: written as a biconditional it made the ADR-0007 rule 4 REOPEN path inexpressible, because a reopened period KEEPS lockedAt. Now one-way: LOCKED demands both audit columns, the audit columns may outlive the lock.

rate_card_versions carried the blanket firstelement_append_only() trigger, which refuses every UPDATE, so RETIRED was unreachable and rate_card_versions_retired_check was dead code. Now firstelement_rate_card_version_guard(): exactly one UPDATE (ACTIVE->RETIRED, fully attributed, successor named, no pricing column moved), DELETE refused.
usage_events shipped append-only by shape only; update usage_events set costAmount succeeded. V20261005090000 now attaches firstelement_append_only() to it.
phase14NewTables: customer_cx_sequences — one row per organizationId holding "lastAllocatedCxSequence" (bigint, CHECK 0..999999), a UNIQUE INDEX arbiter on "organizationId" ALONE (the ON CONFLICT target, not decoration), and a tenant FK with ON DELETE CASCADE. No projectId: a customer's identity is an organization-level thing.
phase14NewFunctions: firstelement_next_customer_cx_id(uuid) RETURNS varchar(9) — the ONLY supported way to obtain a customer reference. ONE statement: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT ("organizationId") DO UPDATE SET "lastAllocatedCxSequence" = <existing> + 1 RETURNING "lastAllocatedCxSequence", then formatted as '#33' || lpad(seq,6,'0'). Marked VOLATILE, contains no count(), and translates a format-ceiling CHECK violation into an operator-readable message while consuming nothing.
phase14Constraints: customers_cxId_key — DROPPED. The GLOBAL UNIQUE INDEX on ("cxId") was ADR-0014 defect CX-1: with a project-scoped count(*) allocator and five retries it limited the whole deployment to five customer references, and the sixth project's first inbound message answered 500 permanently. This is the one DROP in the pair and it replaces a constraint; written without CASCADE, after an explicit pg_constraint.conindid dependency check. Restored to its exact baseline definition by ops/flyway/rollback/undo_phase14.sql.

customers_organizationId_cxId_key — NEW. UNIQUE INDEX ("organizationId", "cxId"), tenant-led by design so it also serves the "this tenant's customer with reference #33000042" lookup. A UNIQUE INDEX and not a UNIQUE CONSTRAINT, so V4's unique_constraints = 0 invariant survives. A unique CONSTRAINT rather than a CHECK, because uniqueness is not expressible in a CHECK.

customer_cx_sequences_sequence_range_check — NEW. CHECK ("lastAllocatedCxSequence" BETWEEN 0 AND 999999): the published `#33` + six digits format of customers."cxId" varchar(9). 1,000,000 references per organization, and the CHECK refuses allocation past it rather than emitting a reference the column cannot hold.
phase14DeliberateDecisions: Per-organization counter, NOT a PostgreSQL SEQUENCE. A global counter makes the total number of customers ever created across ALL tenants inferable from any one tenant's cxId — a cross-tenant information disclosure. Every tenant's first reference is therefore #33000000, which V16 §6e asserts behaviourally.

Plain CREATE UNIQUE INDEX, not CONCURRENTLY. ADR-0005 §3's CONCURRENTLY is unreachable in Flyway Community and ADR-0009 §1 REJECTS spring.flyway.postgresql.transactional-lock=false because it is global and would drop the schema-history lock for the whole chain. At cutover customers holds 3 rows.

Backfill from max("cxId"), never count(*): substr("cxId", 4) is the six-digit sequence, read from rows that still EXIST. It guarantees no LIVE reference is reissued; it CANNOT know about a reference whose holder was deleted before this migration, because nothing in this schema records that. The gap count is reported, not asserted to be zero. Follow-up F-14-1.
Backfill runs BEFORE the uniqueness is relaxed. While the global key holds, max("cxId") is a true high-water mark over everything storable; once it is gone, values at or below it become insertable.

No `version` column on the counter table. Nothing edits a counter except the allocator, which serialises itself with a row lock; a version column would advertise an optimistic-concurrency protocol with no second writer.
phase35Constraints: appointments_created_by_tenant_fkey -- NEW: FOREIGN KEY ("createdById", "organizationId") -> users("id", "organizationId") ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE SET NULL ("createdById").
appointments_customer_tenant_fkey -- NEW: FOREIGN KEY ("customerId", "organizationId") -> customers("id", "organizationId") ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE SET NULL ("customerId").
appointments_doctor_tenant_fkey -- NEW: FOREIGN KEY ("doctorId", "organizationId") -> doctors("id", "organizationId") ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE SET NULL ("doctorId").
appointments_procedure_tenant_fkey -- NEW: FOREIGN KEY ("procedureId", "organizationId") -> procedures("id", "organizationId") ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE SET NULL ("procedureId").

All FOUR pre-existing single-column appointment FKs are KEPT on purpose. They are redundant once the composite exists, but dropping a pre-existing constraint is not this batch's job, and their ON UPDATE CASCADE is propagation behaviour existing code may rely on. The migration asserts all four are still present, so the batch cannot silently remove one.
phase38NewEnumValues: UserRole += CLINIC_STAFF -- one label appended to an EXISTING enum type. Phase 33 named this role in 18 clinic permissions but never added it, so every permission held only by CLINIC_STAFF was held by NOBODY. Adding the label changes the schema fingerprint and no count at all, because enumCount (57) counts enum TYPES rather than labels.
phase38DeliberateDecisions: GRANTS NOBODY. The migration adds a label and rewrites no row. Assigning the role is an operator decision with business context, and a migration that also did it would be inventing one -- the same reason ADR-0009 section 5 makes a migration refuse rather than repair.

ONE STATEMENT, AND IT NEVER USES THE NEW VALUE. PostgreSQL 12 allows ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE inside a transaction block but the new value CANNOT BE USED until that transaction commits; on 11 and earlier the statement itself is rejected. A single statement that never references the value afterwards is correct on both, without the caller needing to know the version. Verified on PostgreSQL 16.15, where the whole DO block succeeds and pg_enum reads back 3 rows.

IF NOT EXISTS, deliberately. Flyway runs a version once, but this chain is also rehearsed against databases restored from backup, and a restore carries the label with it. Without the guard a deployment would abort on a database that is already correct. The Prisma migration for the same change carries the same guard.

REFUSES RATHER THAN REPAIRS, and the refusal was demonstrated firing: against a "UserRole" that already contained an unexpected fourth label the block RAISEd naming it, and pg_enum afterwards still read exactly the original three labels -- the DO block is one transaction, so a refusal leaves nothing behind.

EVERY regtype REFERENCE IS QUALIFIED, after this file failed twice for exactly that reason. `role_type regtype := '"UserRole"'::regtype` is evaluated before the block body and cannot be guarded; under the chain's search_path = '' it resolves to nothing. The unqualified `ALTER TYPE "UserRole"` one line later fails identically. Both errors read only `type "UserRole" does not exist` and name neither this migration nor the cause. See phase38PostBootFingerprint's establishedBy.
phase35DeliberateDecisions: ON DELETE SET NULL with a COLUMN LIST, not the bare form and not CASCADE. The pre-existing appointment FKs are SET NULL (confdeltype = 'n'), NOT CASCADE -- V20261006110000 could copy CASCADE because document_chunks genuinely cascades, and copying it here would DELETE an appointment when its doctor, customer, creator or procedure is removed. The BARE composite form ON DELETE SET NULL is also wrong, and was measured rather than reasoned about: it nulls every referencing column including the NOT NULL organizationId, so 'DELETE FROM doctors' would start FAILING where it previously succeeded. PostgreSQL 15+ accepts ON DELETE SET NULL ("doctorId"), which reproduces the pre-existing behaviour exactly. Verified on PostgreSQL 16.15 in POS-4 of the rehearsal.

Column order is (foreign key column, "organizationId"), which is POSITIONAL. Writing ("organizationId", "doctorId") binds organizationId -> users.id and doctorId -> users.organizationId: not a stricter tenant constraint but a different, wrong one, which rejects every legitimate appointment. The post-condition compares conkey and confkey position by position, and rehearsal control NEG-6 proves a reversed pair is caught.

MATCH SIMPLE (the default), not MATCH FULL. All four appointment columns are nullable, so an appointment may legitimately name no doctor; MATCH SIMPLE leaves it unenforced, MATCH FULL would reject it. Because MATCH SIMPLE also skips the check when organizationId is NULL, the migration ASSERTS appointments.organizationId is still NOT NULL -- that assertion is the tripwire, and rehearsal control NEG-8 proves it fires.

REFUSE, never repair (ADR-0009 section 5). The migration counts cross-tenant appointments against all four references BEFORE the constraint exists and RAISEs naming the offending appointment ids. It deletes no row and rewrites no tenant: choosing which of two scopes was right is a clinical and commercial decision for an operator with the business context. Rehearsal controls NEG-1..NEG-5 demonstrate the refusal firing and prove the offending row SURVIVES the refusal.

No rendered-text assertions. Six guards in this chain compared pg_get_constraintdef output and were broken until Phase 30, because it renders 'REFERENCES doctors(...)' or 'REFERENCES public.doctors(...)' depending on the session search_path. Every assertion here reads conkey/confkey through pg_attribute and compares confrelid to a regclass.
phase35ResidualsReportedNotFixed: F-35-1 appointments.projectId still need not match the project of its doctor, customer, procedure or creating user. appointments.projectId is NOT NULL in the baseline and is not part of the composite pair. Moving a doctor between projects therefore leaves an appointment whose projectId no longer matches its doctor's. Same shape as the residual ADR-0011 section 2 declined to widen (F-2, document_chunks.projectId). NOT shipped: a three-column FK would refuse for a reason nobody authorised.

F-35-2 ON UPDATE CASCADE on the composite pair carries organizationId but NOT projectId. Re-tening a doctor therefore moves its appointments to the new tenant while leaving projectId behind -- the same incompleteness as F-35-1, reached by a different route.

F-35-3 The four redundant single-column FKs are retained on purpose (see phase35DeliberateDecisions). Dropping them is a separate change that must re-measure the appointment delete path first; it is NOT this batch's job.

F-35-4 The ON DELETE CASCADE argument applies to V20261006110000's own precedent as well: any future composite tenant FK added to a table whose existing FKs are SET NULL must use the column-list form, or it will break deletion. The pattern is recorded here rather than only in the migration header.
residualsReportedNotFixed: F-2 document_chunks.projectId need not match documents.projectId: a chunk in tenant A can point at a document in tenant A's OTHER project. Same shape as D2, one column wider. Not shipped because ADR-0011 §2 asks specifically for the (organizationId, id) form and a three-column constraint would refuse for a reason nobody authorised.
F-1 a TENANT-scoped legal hold may still name a projectId. Genuine contradiction, but tightening it is a different change with its own refuse-first argument.
F-3 the LEGACY arm of privacy_deletion_requests_subject_reference_check (CUSTOMER + subjectUserId). Counted by V15 §7b on every bundle run.

F-14-1 the customer reference high-water mark is reconstructible only from SURVIVING customers rows. A customer that once held a reference and has since been deleted leaves no trace — no table records the deletion of a customer reference and nothing foreign-keys on ("cxId") — so max("cxId") can under-report a tenant's true ever-issued maximum. V20261007110000 reports gaps_below_each_tenant_maximum on every run and does NOT assert it to be zero; measured 0 on the verified live database. Fix: an append-only ledger of issued references, seeded once from an export. Until then the allocator is airtight from the moment it starts (V16 §6d proves no reuse after deletion) and the residual is confined to references deleted BEFORE this migration.

The 1,000,000-reference-per-organization format ceiling. customer_cx_sequences_sequence_range_check refuses allocation past #33999999 rather than emitting a reference customers."cxId" varchar(9) cannot hold. That is the published `#33` + six-digit format rather than a design choice, and it is 200000 times the five the defect allowed deployment-wide.

cxIdExists in crm-core is still an UNSCOPED read (ADR-0014 defect list, item 3): it discloses cross-tenant existence through its result and its latency. The schema cannot fix it — the dispatched code change must carry both tenant predicates.
No NOT NULL on the ai_run_* scope columns (ADR-0009 §2 rules 1 and 3). A separate migration, after B1 proves 0 residual NULLs on a disposable copy, with a rehearsed rollback.

undoCheckpoint.note: THREE checkpoints, because the chain now has three removable slices and they must be removed INSIDE OUT: ops/flyway/rollback/undo_phase14.sql FIRST, then undo_phase10b.sql, then undo_phase7_10a.sql. Running them in another order fails, because the Phase-7-10a undo drops ai_approvals, legal_holds and privacy_deletion_requests and the Phase-10b objects on them go with it; at that point undo_phase10b.sql refuses on its partial-batch guard, which is the intended behaviour and not a bug. Each script asserts on the STATE afterwards and raises if its own footprint is not gone; a fingerprint that is anything other than the checkpoint value means something of the slice is left behind. undo_phase14.sql restores customers_cxId_key, which RE-INTRODUCES the CX-1 capacity limit on purpose -- the alternative, a cutover blocked on a schema mistake, is worse. It refuses when two tenants share a reference value (the global key cannot be recreated) and when a counter sits above its tenant's live maximum (references were issued and their holders deleted), so it can only ever succeed on a database where nothing has been issued through Phase 14.
